newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends sharply higher on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends sharply higher on shortcovering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher, with December up sharply on shortcovering.
Traders said the December/March spread widened dramatically as players rolled shorts to March.

"What we saw today was short-covering and a lack of selling tied to the market's perception that the domestic cash basis has firmed over the past 48 hours," a trader said. "Today's price action is a confirmation that we have seen a bottom in this market."
Late gains in KCBT wheat came amid further shortcovering and on spillover strength from CBOT wheat and soybeans.

KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to 16-1/4 cents higher, with December up 16-1/4 cents at $4.40-3/4 a bushel. March gained 11 cents to $4.02-1/4. The December/March spread widened, closing at 38-1/4 cents. It traded late Tuesday at 33 cents.
The last time the nearby KCBT wheat contract closed above $4.40 was Oct 14, when December closed at $4.44-1/2.
CIS sold 2.8 milion March bushels and bought 1.3 million December. Term Commodities sold 1.5 million March. Prudential sold 1.5 million December and bought 1.6 million March.
Prudential also bear-spread one million March/December at 35 to 37-1/2 cents. Benson-Quinn bull-spread 800,000 December/March at 35 to 35-1/2 cents.
